blocks.heading: What this section covers
blocks.text: State the inverse relationship between a good's price and the quantity demanded, show it as a demand schedule and curve, and separate a movement along from a shift of the curve.

blocks.heading: The inverse relationship
blocks.text: When the price of a good rises, the quantity demanded tends to fall; when the price falls, the quantity demanded tends to rise. This inverse relationship holds where nothing else changes: a higher price leaves some buyers unable to pay and turns others towards different goods; a lower price draws new buyers in. A firm that writes down the quantity demanded at each price it might charge has drawn up a demand schedule.

blocks.heading: From schedule to curve
blocks.text: Kaoko Juice's Opuwo schedule: at N$15 a bottle the quantity demanded is 40 bottles a week, at N$12 it is 60 bottles, at N$8 it is 90 bottles. Drawn as a diagram, the price of a bottle goes on the vertical axis and the quantity of bottles on the horizontal, and the demand curve slopes downward through the three points. A kiosk in Sao Paulo in Brazil books the same relationship for bottled water. The curve as a whole is demand itself, not any single point on it.

blocks.heading: A movement, not a shift
blocks.text: When the good's own price changes, the market moves along the demand curve. Cut the price from N$12 to N$8 and the market slides down the same curve from 60 to 90 bottles, because at the lower price more buyers are both willing and able. Nothing outside the price has changed, so the curve stays put: quantity demanded, a point on the curve, has changed; demand, the whole relationship, has not.

blocks.heading: Which axis is which
blocks.text: The confusion learners make: price and quantity are mixed up on the two axes. The boundary: price goes on the vertical axis and quantity on the horizontal, so moving down the curve means a lower price and a larger quantity. The test: label the axes first; a price fall shown as a move up the curve means the axes are wrong.

blocks.heading: Connections
blocks.text: The demand curve is half of the market: topic 2.4 draws the other half, and topic 2.5 joins the two to set the market price.
